memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Enoch had lived 65 years, he became the father of Methuselah. After he became the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked faithfully with God 300 years and had other sons and daughters. - Gen 5:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Suddenly the pattern breaks. For everyone else, the record simply says they "lived" so many years. But of Enoch it says he "walked faithfully with God." That single phrase lifts him out of the crowd. His life was not merely a span of years - it was a walk, a daily companionship with God that lasted three hundred years.

To "walk with God" means to live in close, steady fellowship with Him - going the same direction He goes, keeping in step with Him day by day. It is not a burst of religious enthusiasm but a lifelong journey of trust and obedience. And notice when it deepened: after Enoch became a father. Responsibility and family life did not pull him away from God; they drew him closer.

This is the invitation held out to every believer. Not just to know about God, or to visit Him occasionally, but to walk with Him - through the ordinary and the difficult, year after year.

The New Testament tells us Enoch's walk was really a walk of faith, and that "without faith it is impossible to please God" (Heb 11:5-6). We cannot walk with God on our own strength, but through Christ we are brought near, and by His Spirit we can keep in step with God each day (Gal 5:25). Will you walk with Him?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Would your life be described as "walking with God"?
- What would it look like to keep in step with Him this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I don't just want to know about You - I want to walk with You every day. By Your Spirit, help me keep in step with You through all of life.
